title: Integral compact-support image preserves uniform constructibility

from.place: Proof, sole paragraph: the completed exchange is an isomorphism of integral constructible functors; the constructible landing is the finite-level condition

statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $I=(\varpi)$. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $A_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_T$ and $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $X,Y$ be noetherian schemes (admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) of finite Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $\ell$ invertible on both. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and choose a compactification
$$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y,\qquad pj=f,$$
with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].
For $T=X,Y$, let $\mathcal C_T=\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be exactly the full category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]: its objects are derived $I$-complete, their normalized reduction towers have common bounded adic-lisse finite-type local models, and they admit compatible etale-origin witnesses. Use its inherited triangulated structure [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated].
Identify $A_{\overline X}|_X=A_X$ by restriction to the open subscheme. Let $j_!$ be exact module extension by zero on this localized ringed site, applied degreewise [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and let $Rp_*$ be the completed-coefficient derived module direct image [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Define $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$, the chosen-compactification candidate [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Then $Rf_!^c$ restricts to an exact $A$-linear functor
$$Rf_!^c:\mathcal C_X\longrightarrow\mathcal C_Y$$
[def-weil-linear-functor, def-weil-triangulated-category]. In particular the output belongs to the full compatible uniform category just specified, including its compatible etale-origin witnesses.

Lemma 6.1.13, Lemma 6.7.2, Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.7; completed-coefficient compactification construction and proper preservation. The common-model strengthening uses the existing normalized constructible local-effectivity interface, not an identification by notation.

proof.text: Properness implies that $p$ is finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-cbc-compactification-geometry-fibre-bound] with $T=\overline X$ and the given $Y$. It supplies the Noetherian finite-dimensional ambient scheme, a common bound $e\geq0$ on all geometric fibres of $p$, and invertibility of $\ell$ on $\overline X$. In particular the completed uniform category on $\overline X$ and the proper-preservation theorem below are defined under these scheme hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); Tag 0A3V (lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension), with an explicit common-generator proof also for geometric fibres. Schemes Tags 01I4/01JQ, Properties Tag 04MU; polynomial dimension is the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The coefficient facts used below hold for this finite extension: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] makes $A$ a subring of $E$ and a principal ideal domain with maximal ideal $I$. The extending absolute value is nonarchimedean: after interchanging $x,y$ suppose $|x|_E\leq|y|_E$; if $y\neq0$, then $x/y\in A$ and $1+x/y\in A$, so $|x+y|_E=|y|_E\,|1+x/y|_E\leq|y|_E$, while $y=0$ forces $x=0$. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] holds and it makes every $A/I^n$ finite. In particular $A$ is Noetherian, since each ideal has one generator. Also $\ell\in I$: the extending absolute value satisfies $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, so the maximal-ideal description in the first cited statement applies. Fix $K\in\mathcal C_X$. The implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] supplies a finite stratification and the perfect $A$-complex models needed for extension by zero.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Lemma 6.1.12, used through the cited compatible-uniform characterization and arbitrary-ringed open-closed statements; Stacks Tags 01J3, 09AA, 09BN, 09AH, 03DI and 03DJ.

proof.text: Put $J=j_!K$. Identify the open site with the localized site by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Apply [lem-cbc-extension-zero-stratified-perfect] to the models of step 2. A closed subscheme with the complementary support exists by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]; the lemma gives the old perfect models and the zero model on that complement. Thus condition (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] holds on $\overline X$. The implication (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i), with the scheme hypotheses of step 1, gives $J\in\mathcal C_{\overline X}$, including the common normalized models and compatible etale-origin witnesses of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete].

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Lemma 6.1.12, used through the cited compatible-uniform characterization and arbitrary-ringed open-closed statements; Stacks Tags 01J3, 09AA, 09BN, 09AH, 03DI and 03DJ.

proof.text: The same characterization [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], now using (i)$\Rightarrow$(iii), says that $J$ is bounded. Choose $u\leq v$ with $\mathcal H^q(J)=0$ outside $[u,v]$; for the zero object any interval suffices. For every $n\geq1$, [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] gives the two-term resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A]$ of $P_n=A/I^n$ in degrees $[-1,0]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], its completed constant realization $[A_{\overline X}\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A_{\overline X}]$ is a flat resolution of $(P_n)_{\overline X}$. Consequently the underlying completed-coefficient complex of the canonical reduction $J_n$ is the cone of $\varpi^n:J\to J$. In the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], its degree-$q$ cohomology is between $\mathcal H^q(J)$ and $\mathcal H^{q+1}(J)$, so it vanishes for $q<u-1$ or $q>v$. Restriction of scalar structure does not change a module sheaf's zero object or its cohomology groups. Hence all canonical $J_n$ have the one cohomological interval $[u-1,v]$, independently of $n$.

source.place: Tags 093M (lemma-completion-flat) and 093J (lemma-constant-exact); the stated two-term quotient resolution and the cohomology sequence of its tensor cone. Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 6.8.11(3) supplies the bounded description through the cited characterization.

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-preservation-constructible] to the identity base-change square for $p:\overline X\to Y$: both vertical maps are $p$, and the horizontal maps are the identities of $\overline X$ and $Y$. The square is cartesian, and both vertical maps are proper. All four scheme entries are Noetherian and finite-dimensional by step 1 and the hypotheses. Take its integer $N=\ell$: it is positive, kills $A/I$, and is invertible on $Y$ and $\overline X$. The common geometric-fibre bound is the $e$ of step 1. The input $J$ belongs to the exact compatible uniform category by step 3, and its reductions have the common interval $[u-1,v]$ by step 4. Thus the first conclusion of that preservation theorem gives $Rp_*J\in\mathcal C_Y$ (indeed its reductions have cohomology in $[u-1,v+2e]$). This is membership in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], including compatible etale-origin witnesses; it is not just levelwise constructibility. Since $J=j_!K$, [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] identifies this object with precisely the chosen candidate $Rf_!^cK$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.7; the precise uniform-and-witness conclusion is the cited existing proper preservation theorem. The finite-level sources are Stacks Tag 0GL0 (theorem-constructible-shriek) and Tag 095U (lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper).

proof.text: The coefficient identification [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], applied to the finite rings $A/I^n$ from step 2, makes the direct image the module functor of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Its K-injective construction is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]; these are exactly the operations used by [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. For extension by zero apply [lem-cbc-localized-extension-zero-linear-derived] to $\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $A\to A_{\overline X}$: it gives the additive $A$-linear termwise functor with its shifts and triangles. The direct-image functor is additive and $A$-linear on the complete inputs $J$ of step 3 by [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange]. Their composite therefore commutes with shifts, preserves triangles, and preserves sums and scalar multiples of morphisms between the inputs under consideration.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI/03DJ; proetale.tex Tag 099N for the completed direct image; the existing generic derived-functor triangulation and linear-derived-category nodes supply the categorical facts.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 5 put the objects of the composite in the required full subcategories. Fullness restricts all its maps with no choices. By [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated], the two subcategories inherit their shifts and distinguished triangles from the ambient categories. The shift comparison of step 6 therefore restricts. An input distinguished triangle is sent to an ambient distinguished triangle with all three vertices in $\mathcal C_Y$, hence to a distinguished triangle there. Together with the additive and scalar equations in step 6 this gives the exact $A$-linear functor $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ for this fixed compactification.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N5-9a81aaedd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all three new nodes in full, every cited statement, and the sources: Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.1.12, Proposition 6.6.11, Lemma 6.7.2, Definition 6.7.6/Lemma 6.7.7; Stacks 0A3V, 01T6, 03DI/03DJ, 09AA/09BN; the blueprint thm-cbc-finite-extension, identical in master and main-20261015. The repair fixes the return: the steps are now 478–1115 characters and each extracted argument is a genuine smaller lemma, not a restated clause. Steps 1–7 check: the geometry lemma gives Noetherian finite-dimensional X̄, the geometric-fibre bound e and ℓ invertible. The DVR facts give the finite quotients A/I^n and ℓ in I. The characterization's (i)⇒(ii) on X, the model lemma, then (ii)⇒(i) on X̄ give J in C_X̄ with its witnesses. The cone of ϖ^n gives the uniform interval [u-1,v]. Preservation applied to the identity square (N=ℓ, fibre bound e) gives Rp_*J in C_Y. Linearity comes from the new extension-by-zero lemma plus lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange on complete objects, and step 7 restricts to full triangulated subcategories. The coefficient category is the completed A_T throughout; no constant-coefficient comparison and no SGA source is used. All 11 declared tool uses are accepted. No missing or merged ids, no cycles, citers unaffected. New-node checks: the geometry lemma is true and not a duplicate (lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound covers only ordinary fibres); the stratified-model lemma is true, since the stratification definition needs only a disjoint locally closed cover, j^{-1}j_! is the identity and i^{-1}j_! is zero; the linear extension-by-zero lemma is true, and Mathlib's derived-linearity instance assumes linearity rather than proving it, so it is not a leaf. Edge cases tested: empty schemes, U empty or U=T, K=0, A=0.
